title: Health: A User's Guide: You have a part to play in your own care. Scripts included.
description: Your doctor expects you to choose. Your insurer expects you to appeal. Nobody told you. Health care is two things at once, and this book shows you how to get the best from both. The people who care for you. The nurse, the doctor and the pharmacist mostly want what you want, and they do their best work for a patient who arrives prepared. The book is the preparation: what to bring and what to ask, so a short visit covers what matters; how to hear a risk, a test result or a prognosis in plain numbers; and what to ask before an operation, in the hospital, and before you go home. The system they work in. Around them runs an industry that pays people you never meet to decide what you use and what you pay: the reviewer who decides whether care was necessary, the coder who decides what your visit was, the collector who decides how many times you'll be asked. They have a revenue maximizer. Who is your cost minimizer? A tax-exempt hospital must offer to cut the bills of patients who can't pay; about three in ten of them ever get the discount. In Medicare Advantage, about one denial in nine is appealed, and eight in ten of those appeals win in full or in part. People who call about a bill they think is wrong get it corrected about three times in four. Inside: What to prepare before a visit, and the questions that change a decision How to ask about risk in people, not percentages, before a test or an operation What to ask before surgery, on the first day in hospital, and before you're sent home Your medicines, a serious diagnosis, pain, pregnancy, children, and your parents Which door to use, from telehealth to the emergency room, and what each one costs How to hold a bill until it's itemized, and apply for the discount the hospital must offer How to appeal a denial, step by step,

title: The Care Talk: Scripts for Conversations With Aging Parents (VIBESVITAL Talk Series Book 5
description: You've noticed something — your parent seems less steady, the mail is piling up, a phone call felt off. You've thought about bringing it up. You've also found a dozen reasons not to. The Care Talk gives you the exact words for the conversations adult children keep putting off — driving, health, living arrangements, finances, and the scams that specifically target older adults. Not a legal guide. Not a medical guide. The sentences that help you start, when starting is the hardest part. Inside, you'll find: Core scripts for opening these conversations with care, not confrontation Scripts for driving, health changes, living arrangements, and finances A full chapter on recognizing and discussing financial scams Coordinating caregiving fairly among siblings Advance directives and end-of-life wishes, handled with care Assisted living and memory care transitions Caregiver burnout, setting limits, and downsizing the family home Twelve real composite conversations showing these scripts in action A quick-reference index of every script in the book Whether you're just starting to notice changes or already deep into caregiving, this book gives you the words to have these conversations earlier, calmer, and together. This book offers communication guidance only, not legal, medical, or financial advice. For legal matters such as power of attorney or advance directives, consult an elder law attorney. For health and capacity concerns, consult a doctor. title: How to Let Go of Toxic Friendships: 5 Short Scripts to End a Friendship with Clarity and C
description: Have you stayed too long in a friendship that quietly hurt you? If you’ve ever left a hangout feeling drained, replayed subtle digs in your head, or dreaded replying to a message but felt guilty not to, you are not alone. Friendships are supposed to feel mutual, safe, and supportive, but sometimes they don’t. This booklet is here to help. What You’ll Get Inside In How to Let Go of Toxic Friendships , you’ll discover five short, ready-to-use scripts that guide you through fading out, resetting, or saying goodbye clearly and kindly. Each script is designed to sound respectful, steady, and compassionate, and can be adapted for text, email, or in-person conversations. You’ll also find: A quick self-test to recognize unhealthy friendship patterns The neuroscience of why friendship endings feel so hard Guidance for choosing between a gentle fade or a direct conversation Body language and delivery tips for steady goodbyes A printable summary you can screenshot and keep close Why It Works This booklet is not about drama or burning bridges. It is about releasing what no longer serves you with honesty and care. Backed by psychology and real-life examples, it helps you protect your peace, grieve what was good, and make room for healthier friendships to come. About the Series How to Let Go of Toxic Friendships is Booklet 4 in the Crisis Script Series, a set of practical and emotionally intelligent guides that provide short scripts for life’s hardest conversations. This title is part of the Relationship Clarity Collection, one of four themed collections within the series. Each booklet can be read on its own, or alongside the others for a complete toolkit. You are not cruel for letting go. You are choosing peace. Learn how to step away from toxic friendships with clarity and compassi

description: 136 Real Japanese Scenarios for Clinics, Hospitals and Pharmacies You're sick in Japan. The receptionist hands you a form entirely in Japanese. title: Professional Clinical Communication Scripts: The Complete 5-Volume Series
description: The Clinical Communication Scripts series is a practical, evidence-based toolkit designed for nurse practitioners, physicians, and allied health professionals who deliver care through telehealth. Each volume focuses on one of the most challenging conversation types clinicians face — from de-escalating hostile encounters and delivering difficult diagnoses, to conducting mental health risk assessments, navigating controlled substance requests, and guiding end-of-life discussions. Inside every volume you’ll find a recognized communication framework, step-by-step sample scripts, and a concise do’s and don’ts checklist you can reference before any high-stakes visit. title: Make Your Script Sellable : The Art and Business of Screenwriting
description: Cara J. Russell is a prolific screenwriter with a background in journalism. Her movies can currently be seen on Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hallmark Channel, Hallmark Drama, Lifetime, UPtv, PixL TV, and more. As of this writing, she has 10 + screenplay projects in development with various producers and production companies. In addition to her screenwriting, Cara works as a Creative Development Executive for MPCA (Motion Picture Corporation of America), a film production company in Los Angeles that is a world-leading producer of Christmas and family-themed movies and television entertainment. As a Creative Development Executive, Cara has read and given extensive notes on hundreds of scripts. She works on the production side of film and TV projects for networks and streamers from the initial pitches through the shooting drafts. A large part of her job is working with writers and helping them get their scripts into sellable shape for buyers such as Netflix, Hallmark Channel, Hallmark Movies and Mysteries, Paramount, ABC, CBS, HBO Plus, NBC Peacock, Disney Plus, Lifetime, and many more. Working on both sides of the table gives Cara a unique perspective. She found herself giving the same notes over and over again to new writers and decided to write a screenwriting book. The purpose of this book is to help screenwriters who already understand basic structure and story elements but their scripts need a lot more work to get them into sellable shape. Cara explains the notes that are commonly given to writers by Development Executives on their submitted scripts to help you identify and solve those issues before you submit your script to a production company or studio. Knowing the right people, people who are willing to read your spec and/or are looking to hire writers for open writing

title: Mascara Ministry: A Devotional for Women Who Love Skincare, Self-Care & Scripture
description: Mascara Ministry is a devotional for women who love beauty, self-care, and Scripture — and who want to grow deeper in faith while caring well for themselves in everyday life. This book invites you into thoughtful moments that blend everyday beauty routines with faith-filled reflection. Each chapter pairs practical skincare and makeup habits with spiritual encouragement, helping you slow down, reflect, and grow — not just in appearance, but in purpose. Inside, you’ll find: • Beauty routines that encourage consistency, care, and simplicity • Faith reflections designed to spark personal insight or group discussion • Guided prayers to help center your heart and spirit • Space for journaling through Your Minutes and capturing meaning in Your Moment The beauty tips are offered for inspiration, not perfection — you may already have routines that work well for you. What matters most is faithfulness in the small, daily choices. The spiritual reflections are meant to open conversation, deepen understanding, and encourage continued growth in your walk with God. Whether used personally or in a small group setting, Mascara Ministry is a gentle reminder that true beauty is cultivated over time — through intention, grace, and a life rooted in faith.
